pass_rule: verifiers with the order or the version check execute no replayed command; the full verifier with a right or slow clock, with or without the TTL, executes every committed command and never deviates from the reference; the signature-only verifier does execute replays of reversed and old commands
known_issues: C and D are the same here: the attack does not depend on who runs the validators. A and B's centre-signed commands go through the same checks (tests/test_verifier.py), not this experiment.
no message loss: every honest copy arrives, so a committed command can fail only by a check; with loss a stale state report can also hold a command back for one slot (tests/test_lasthop.py)
RotatingDispatch stands in for policy.py; the commands follow the substations' state reports on the chain, so a replay that flips a feeder is undone at the next dispatch slot at the latest
an attacker who also withholds deliveries and releases them late is not in this experiment: only the TTL stops that, and only with a right clock
a replay of the newest block is dropped as a copy of the trusted header, without an event (column ignored_duplicate)
